text.p: The following are the reports carried by Estonia's newspapers on Wednesday. Reuters has not verified these reports and does not vouch for their accuracy:
- The leaders of Tallinna Bank and Union Bank signed a statement halting their war of words, and apologised to each other, their clients and the public.
- The government approved a draft law restricting the circulation of pornographic material.

- Estonia needs four to six light fighter aircraft for controlling its airspace in peacetime, the commander of the country's defence forces Johannes Kert said on his return from a meeting with his Lithuanian and Latvian counterparts in Riga.
-A bomb exploded in a car in Tallinn's Pirita suburb. No one was hurt.
- The presidents of Estonia, Latvia, Lithuania, Ukraine and Poland will meet in Tallinn on May 25 to discuss economic cooperation and European integration, the foreign ministry said.
- General Motors granted the Supplier of the Year award to Estonia's Norma, which makes safety belts for GM.
- Russia repeated its warning that its agreement with NATO could be reconsidered if the Baltic countries are offered membership in the alliance.
- Estonian computer firm Microlink will open a plant to produce cables in June.
